primary_metric: Macro mean recovery@16 over cases after averaging seeds; the forced-backbone hierarchical skeleton versus the frozen parent-strata v1 cells (official, unstratified, edge_count, parent_set) and the frozen skeleton_complete cells.
split_rule: Identical case IDs, seeds, budget, sampling and seed schedule as the frozen parent-strata v1 protocol, so every skeleton cell pairs with the recorded v1 cells on the same case and seed. Only the two new variants use fresh model inference; the four controls are the frozen v1 raw calls and the skeleton_complete cells are the frozen parent-skeleton v1 run.
dev_decision: On the frozen dev split, skeleton_complete_forced reached R 21.91% versus 18.34% for skeleton_complete, 13.36% for parent_set and 4.25% for edge_count/unstratified, recovering 3/7 truths on n2_169 where complete recovered 2/7. skeleton_complete_limit (budget enforcement only, no forced backbone) reached 18.34%, so the forced backbone is the active component on dev. Both variants were frozen before any test inference.
method_definition: Each attempt cycles over the a-priori parent-set strata of the most ambiguous anchor (same cycle as parent-strata v1). skeleton_complete_forced presents the stratum parents plus every forced edge (an edge whose removal from the allowed supergraph disconnects a required path, hence present in every compatible graph) as already-fixed direct edges; the model outputs only the remaining edges it adds. skeleton_complete_limit keeps the skeleton_complete wording. Both variants enforce the public edge budget during assembly: later model additions are dropped in parsed order while the union exceeds max_edges; fixed edges are never dropped. No coverage feedback, no graph-edit actions, no change to the edge-list representation.
